day-61-act-01.title: Instruction Dataset Schemas: Alpaca, ChatML, and ShareGPT Multi-Turn Conventions
day-61-act-01.prerequisites: Completion of Day 60 foundational pre-training assessment and Python JSON data modeling.
day-61-act-01.objective: Master the structural schemas of instruction datasets, distinguishing between Alpaca single-turn format, ChatML role delimiters, and ShareGPT multi-turn conversational trees.
day-61-act-01.instructions:
Study source: within this activity's existing reading/practice time, use Hugging Face LLM Course: Fine-tuning LLMs, Chapter 11.2: Common Template Formats; Hands-on Exercise, then explain one connection to the local task in your own words. Keep the local exercise and acceptance checks; use its original explanation if the external source is unavailable. 1. Inspect Stanford Alpaca schema: top-level keys 'instruction' (task description), 'input' (optional context), and 'output' (target response).
2. Contrast with ChatML markup format: structured text wrapped in explicit demarcation tokens (<|im_start|>system...<|im_end|>, <|im_start|>user...<|im_end|>, <|im_start|>assistant...<|im_end|>).
3. Analyze ShareGPT multi-turn schema: a list of message objects under 'conversations' with alternating 'from' ('human'/'gpt') and 'value' fields.
4. Understand why ambiguous plain text delimiters (such as 'User: ... Assistant:') suffer from prompt injection and delimiter hijacking, whereas dedicated boundary tokens enforce strict role sandboxing.
day-61-act-01.exercise_prompt: Write a Python normalization function normalize_to_chatml(record) that detects whether a record is Alpaca format or ShareGPT format and returns a canonical list of message dictionaries [{'role': ..., 'content': ...}]. Test with both empty and populated 'input' fields.
day-61-act-01.hint: For Alpaca with an 'input' field, combine 'instruction' and 'input' into the user message, or structure 'instruction' as system context and 'input' as user query.
day-61-act-01.mastery_criterion: Write a schema normalization pipeline that converts both Alpaca and ShareGPT records to verified ChatML message structures with 100% field compliance.

day-61-act-02.title: Tokenizer Special Tokens, Delimiters, and Boundary Alignment
day-61-act-02.prerequisites: Day 61 Activity 1 and Byte-Pair Encoding tokenization mechanics.
day-61-act-02.objective: Add new special tokens (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>) to tokenizers, prevent sub-token fragmentation, and diagnose token boundary alignment hazards.
day-61-act-02.instructions:
1. Examine how standard tokenizers split unknown delimiter strings into multiple subword tokens when delimiters are not registered as special tokens.
2. Use tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens': ['<|im_start|>', '<|im_end|>']}) and inspect model embedding resize requirements.
3. Verify token boundary alignment: ensure special tokens are encoded as single discrete token IDs and decode cleanly without injecting spurious whitespace.
4. Diagnose the space-prefix issue in BPE: note how ' hello' vs 'hello' encode differently and ensure chat templates format newline and role separators consistently.
day-61-act-02.exercise_prompt: Implement a test script that takes a tokenizer, adds '<|im_start|>' and '<|im_end|>', encodes '<|im_start|>user\nHello<|im_end|>', and asserts that the first and last tokens are the exact registered special token IDs of length 1 each.
day-61-act-02.hint: Check tokenizer.encode('<|im_start|>', add_special_tokens=False). It must return a single integer ID matching tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|im_start|>').
day-61-act-02.answer:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
def verify_special_tokens(tokenizer_name_or_path='gpt2'):
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(tokenizer_name_or_path)
    num_added = tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens': ['<|im_start|>', '<|im_end|>']})
    encoded = tokenizer.encode('<|im_start|>user\nHello<|im_end|>', add_special_tokens=False)
    start_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|im_start|>')
    end_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|im_end|>')
    assert encoded[0] == start_id, f'Expected start token {start_id}, got {encoded[0]}'
    assert encoded[-1] == end_id, f'Expected end token {end_id}, got {encoded[-1]}'
    return True
day-61-act-02.mastery_criterion: Verify special token boundary integrity, ensuring zero sub-word fragmentation for ChatML delimiter tokens.

day-61-act-03.title: Multi-Turn Dialogue Serialization and System Prompt Conditioning
day-61-act-03.prerequisites: Day 61 Activities 1 and 2, Jinja2 templating syntax.
day-61-act-03.objective: Render multi-turn conversational histories into linear token sequences using Jinja2 chat templates and implement safe conversation truncation that preserves system context.
day-61-act-03.instructions:
1. Formulate a Jinja2 chat template that wraps system, user, and assistant turns with ChatML delimiters (<|im_start|>role\ncontent<|im_end|>\n).
2. Study tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False/True) and understand how add_generation_prompt=True appends '<|im_start|>assistant\n' for inference.
3. Address the context-window overflow problem: when a multi-turn dialogue exceeds maximum sequence length (e.g., 2048 tokens), implement intelligent truncation.
4. Design truncation to strictly preserve the system prompt (turn 0) while pruning oldest user-assistant interaction turns first.
day-61-act-03.exercise_prompt: Build a function truncate_dialogue(messages, max_tokens, tokenizer) that serializes messages with a ChatML template and prunes earliest user/assistant pairs until total encoded token length is <= max_tokens, keeping any system prompt intact.
day-61-act-03.hint: Separate system messages from conversational history. If total tokens > max_tokens, pop the earliest user and assistant turns (indices 0 and 1 of history) in pairs.
day-61-act-03.mastery_criterion: Demonstrate intelligent conversation truncation that preserves system prompt integrity while strictly respecting sequence length limits.

day-61-act-04.title: Independent Assessment: Production ChatML Normalization and Token Boundary Validator
day-61-act-04.objective: Build a production-grade dataset validation and formatting pipeline that normalizes heterogeneous raw records, verifies special token delimiters, and detects schema corruption.
day-61-act-04.instructions:
1. Create a Python module ChatMLDatasetValidator.
2. Accept a mixed JSON/JSONL dataset containing Alpaca, ShareGPT, and raw ChatML formats.
3. Validate that every record contains valid role sequences (system prompt if present must be first, alternating user/assistant turns, non-empty content).
4. Apply ChatML tokenization and assert that delimiters occupy exactly single token IDs.
5. Output an audit summary reporting valid samples, malformed records filtered out, and token length distribution statistics.
day-61-act-04.exercise_prompt: Run ChatMLDatasetValidator against a test batch of 10 records containing 2 malformed records (e.g. missing assistant response, consecutive user turns). Confirm that invalid records are caught and valid records are serialized correctly.
day-61-act-04.hint: Check alternating roles by verifying messages[i]['role'] != messages[i-1]['role'] for conversational turns.
day-61-act-04.mastery_criterion: Deliver an independent validator identifying 100% of malformed dialogue schemas and formatting valid records without tokenization artifacts.
